stories.headline: Meta's largest open model reads code, images, audio, and video at once
stories.summary: Meta's Muse Spark Open is an 816B-parameter mixture-of-experts model that activates only 42B parameters per token, built for agentic coding across text, images, audio, and video. Weights and fine-tuning recipes are public on Hugging Face. It needs 32 H200 GPUs in BF16, setting the hardware floor for self-hosted frontier coding agents.
stories.take: Open-weight frontier coding agents required proprietary APIs; Meta's 816B model puts that capability on your own hardware.

stories.headline: Financial agent safety depends on where controls sit, not how many
stories.summary: At AI Engineer New York, OpenAI, Anthropic, Two Sigma, and Bloomberg converged on one principle: agent safety in finance is a placement problem, not a restriction count. Two Sigma runs five composable controls, each doing one job, routing only the highest-stakes decisions to humans. The question for your deployment: where does your approval layer sit, and who designed it?
stories.take: Financial firms treated agent safety as a restriction problem; placement of controls is the real variable.

claims.summary_span: Financial agent safety depends on where controls sit, not how many

claims.note: Direct paraphrase of the source's stated main lesson.

claims.source_span: One of the key themes at the AI Engineer New York conference this week was how to balance agent autonomy with security and safety. Both frontier labs and financial firms focused on this issue in their presentations this week. The main lesson: safe autonomy depends on where you put controls and human judgment, rather than how many restrictions you impose.
claims.note: All four named entities presented at AIE New York per the source, and the shared principle is accurately paraphrased.

stories.headline: AI voice fraud cost Italy's biggest bank €95 million
stories.summary: Fraudsters impersonating Fideuram executives used AI-generated voice or messaging to steal €95 million from Intesa Sanpaolo's private banking arm, two anonymous sources told Reuters. No systems breach; the attack vector was identity, not infrastructure. If your payment-authorisation chain relies on voice confirmation from senior leaders, who in your org can actually verify the caller is real?

stories.headline: A language model caught loan policy breaches human reviewers missed
stories.summary: An arXiv preprint describes a two-step prototype: extract compliance rules from policy documents into structured form, then score each application against them. Tested on 11 real corporate loans with known exceptions, it caught the majority and surfaced issues human reviewers had missed. When does your credit team pilot this against its own policy library?
stories.take: Manual loan-policy review was the only option; a prototype now flags exceptions human reviewers overlooked.

stories.summary: Ollama 0.40.5 ships NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Super, a vision-language model with 1M-token context, tool calling, and a switchable reasoning mode. The smaller Bolt variant (74B parameters, 9B active) fits a 24GB GPU with speculative decoding built in. Run `ollama run nemotron-3.5-super` against your current local agentic stack; the 1M-token window is the real test.

stories.headline: Nubank doubled training throughput by fixing attention kernels and compiler setup
stories.summary: Nubank's engineering blog details how switching to cuDNN attention kernels and fixing compiler graph breaks lifted training efficiency from 21% to 39% on a hybrid architecture. No single architectural change drove the gain; kernel selection alone added 7 percentage points. Audit your own training stack's kernel selection before your next experiment cycle.
stories.take: Transformer training budgets assumed kernel defaults were optimal; Nubank's production run proves they rarely are.

claims.note: The source title says '~2× MFU' and the MFU roughly doubles (21→39%), so 'doubled throughput' is a supported approximation; attention kernels and compiler fixes are the named mechanisms.

stories.headline: A pre-trained model that resizes itself to fit any hardware budget
stories.summary: Fixed model sizes force a hardware commitment at deployment. An arXiv preprint converts any pre-trained transformer into one elastic checkpoint that trims neurons and attention heads on demand, reaching 1.8× throughput at 60% sparsity with under 1% accuracy loss. The code is public and the published benchmark covers accuracy and throughput across five sparsity levels.
stories.take: Inference sizing required committing to a fixed model family; one elastic checkpoint now spans the full compute range.

stories.headline: A reinforcement-learning system reads finance papers to build trading signals
stories.summary: AlphaRLM, an arXiv preprint, trains a language model via reinforcement learning to read financial research papers and construct executable trading factors without seed expressions. Tested on CSI 300, CSI 1000, and S&P 500, the 8-billion-parameter model beats established baselines on annualised excess return. The cross-market results remain preliminary findings in a preprint, not a validated deployment framework.
stories.take: Quant factor discovery required human researchers; a trained language model now reads the literature directly.

stories.headline: Databricks cuts the networking tax on serverless data workloads
stories.summary: More than 75% of Databricks customers cited network complexity as the reason workloads stayed on classic compute. Private Network Gateway replaces per-resource load balancers and proxy VMs with a single delegated subnet, routing all serverless traffic through your existing firewall. Public preview on Azure; AWS in private preview. Public preview on Azure makes the gateway available to test today.
stories.take: Serverless networking required per-resource proxy deployments; one delegated subnet now covers everything.
